newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-REDS' PENDLETON UNDERGOES KNEE SURGERY.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-REDS' PENDLETON UNDERGOES KNEE SURGERY.

text.p: Terry Pendleton's plans to break into the Cincinnati Reds lineup suffered a setback when the former National League Most Valuable Player underwent knee surgery.

Pendleton, who signed a minor league contract with the Reds after the Atlanta Braves elected not to re-sign him, had surgery to repair torn cartilage in his right knee Wednesday night. He sustained the injury before the team's first exhibition game and is expected to be sidelined three to six weeks.
Pendleton hit .238 with 11 homers and 75 RBI for the Florida Marlins and Atlanta Braves last season. He hit just .204 in 42 games for Atlanta.
The 36-year-old Pendleton is a career .271 hitter with 136 homers and 900 RBI in 13 major league seasons with the St. Louis Cardinals, Atlanta and Florida.
In 1991, during his first stint with the Braves, Pendleton batted a career-high .319 with 22 home runs and 86 RBI, earning National League MVP honours.

A three-time Gold Glove winner and an All-Star in 1992, Pendleton played for the losing team in five World Series. He lost the World Series with St Louis in 1985 and 1987, and with Atlanta in 1991, 1992 and 1996.
